_comment: Next Bar T0 surface. Until this file existed, tier-classify.mjs fell back to
the generic defaults, which declare NO T0 globs at all — so migrations and the
account-deletion path both classified T1 and the T0 gate could never fire.
Every T0 rule below must match at least one real file; run
`git ls-files | node ~/.claude/bin/tier-classify.mjs --validate` after editing,
because a dead T0 glob silently leaves a path unprotected.
escalate_min_t0_files was 5 until 2026-07-31. That was indefensible here: ONE
migration file is already irreversible without a restore, and restore capability
is UNVERIFIED. A change touching four T0 files would not have escalated. Now 1.
Rules resolve to the HIGHEST matching tier, not first- or last-match, so a
stricter rule always wins and rule order does not matter.
Glob the code that PERFORMS a destructive act, not just its entry point:
prune-orphan-photos.mjs was T0 while scripts/lib/photoFiles.mjs — which holds
the actual unlink loop — was T1, a gate you escape by refactoring.
PORTED to chore/prime-foundation 2026-08-07 from 775c0b7 (feat/overnight-2026-07-30).
This file was never merged to main, so origin/main had NO project tier policy at
all and the overnight preflight failed closed. Two T0 rules were dropped in the
port — scripts/lib/photoFiles.mjs and scripts/prune-orphan-photos.mjs — because
neither file exists on this base (there is no scripts/lib/ here), and the
validator rejects a rule matching no tracked file. Nothing on THIS tree is left
unprotected by the drop. But the intent must not be lost: the repository-owned
classifier must carry a BAKED-IN T0 floor for file-deleting scripts, so that
re-adding a photo-prune path here cannot land as T1. That is a required case for
the Item 1 classifier work — do not close Item 1 without it.
KNOWN STRUCTURAL GAP — read before trusting this file. Independent review on
2026-08-07 (Claude/FABLE, GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, converging) established
that EVERY T0 rule here is a PATH ENUMERATION. There is no pattern rule and no
behavioural catch-all. Therefore ANY NEW FILE AT AN UNLISTED PATH LANDS AT T1,
no matter how destructive. Confirmed evasions, none of which this file catches:
- a new scripts/purge-photos.mjs calling fs.unlinkSync            -> T1
- a new scripts/cleanup-accounts.mts with delete from auth.users  -> T1
- a new src/app/api/admin/purge/route.ts with a DELETE handler    -> T1
- supabase/functions/** (edge functions, service-role, raw SQL)   -> T1, uncovered
- next.config.ts (CSP headers, rewrites past middleware)          -> T1, uncovered
- a new service-role client in src/lib/**                         -> T1, uncovered
- package.json / lockfile (supply chain)                          -> T1, uncovered
The auth.users-delete pattern was recognised in TWO specific files and never
generalised. Splitting dangerous work across two T1 files also yields an
aggregate T1: there is no transitive-impact rule, so a new dependency OF a T0
file is itself only T1.
This is NOT fixed here, deliberately. The fix is a repository-owned classifier
with a BAKED-IN T0 FLOOR that fails closed on unknown paths — which is exactly
the Item 1 deliverable (goal g-134e4680). Patching more enumerated globs into
this file would be whack-a-mole and would give false confidence. Until Item 1
lands, treat a T1 result on a NEW file as UNVERIFIED, not as safe.

rules.note: Schema and grants against live user data. Applying one is irreversible without a restore, and 0034-style grant changes can lock every user out of their own rows. Attended window only.
Fresh-project bootstrap schema — same blast radius as a migration.

Destructive and irreversible: deletes an auth user and cascades through every table they own. NOTE: this used to claim it was 'the one route holding the service-role key'. That was FALSE — src/app/api/event/route.ts also constructs a service-role client. Corrected 2026-07-31 after a review panel caught it.

The SECOND service-role route. Bypasses RLS, and is triggerable by an unauthenticated POST — the allowlist on the event name is the only control. Missed on the first pass because the map's own note asserted account/delete was the only service-role holder.
Executes a chosen migration as raw SQL against DATABASE_URL. Same blast radius as apply-migrations.ts, which was already T0 — this sibling was simply not globbed.
Sets ANY user's password via the Supabase admin API and confirms their email, bypassing the email flow entirely. That is account takeover as a supported operator tool.

Executes `delete from auth.users where id = $1` against DATABASE_URL (line 136). It is meant to clean up a user it just created, but the id is computed at runtime and DATABASE_URL is whatever the environment points at — a regression in that id, or a misaimed env, deletes a REAL user and cascades through every table they own. Same blast radius as src/app/api/account/delete/**, which is already T0. Found 2026-08-07 by the Codex review lane; the ported map classified it T1 with no escalation.

Second script executing `delete from auth.users where id = $1` against DATABASE_URL (line 151). Same reasoning as rpc-smoke.mts. Two independent scripts holding an unguarded auth.users delete is exactly the 'glob the code that PERFORMS the destructive act' rule this file already states.

`fs.unlinkSync(src)` in a loop over produced files (line 87) — deletes the ORIGINAL JPEGs after conversion. This is the surviving instance of the photo-deletion surface that prune-orphan-photos.mjs and scripts/lib/photoFiles.mjs used to cover; those two do not exist on this base, but this one does and was unprotected. An over-broad `produced` set destroys source media with no undo.

Calls billable Google Places APIs across the catalog. Proposed as T0 and DEMOTED to T1 on adjudication: T0 in this map means irreversible destruction or takeover with no undo. A runaway bill is bounded, self-limiting (quotas, budget alerts) and recoverable; a dropped table with an unverified restore is not. Putting cost in the same tier devalues the label for the changes that can actually end the project. FOLLOW-UP, not fixed here: the script issues API requests BEFORE the --apply guard, so a dry run still spends. That is a one-line correctness bug and wants a MAX_CALLS cap — fixing it is the right control, not tier weight.

Runs `update auth.users set email_confirmed_at = now() where email = $1` against DATABASE_URL (line 63) — the same primitive that made rpc-smoke.mts and nights-smoke.mts T0. Deliberately held at T1, recorded so nobody has to re-derive it: the target is a HARDCODED literal (nextbar.test.sam@example.com, line 24), not a runtime-computed id; the operation is a reversible UPDATE rather than a DELETE; and the script self-guards with `if (process.env.LOOP_UNATTENDED === '1') exit` (line 16). Same adjudication as refresh-places.mjs below — T0 here means irreversible destruction or takeover with no undo, and diluting it devalues the label for changes that can actually end the project. Raised by the Claude/FABLE review lane 2026-08-07; made explicit rather than left to default_tier.

NOT documentation, despite the .md extension: these are the operating instructions the coding agent follows for this repository. A change here can tell the agent to skip a gate, so it must never inherit the blanket **/*.md T2. Rules resolve to the HIGHEST matching tier, so this overrides that glob.
Runs BEFORE every matched route handler, so no per-route control can gate it. A wrong matcher is an un-gateable amplification lever (C2 F1b).
The runner that applies schema changes to a live database, including the drift check that refuses an edited-after-apply file.
Rate limiting for every public route. Not T0 — it cannot destroy data — but a regression here removes the only abuse control the public surface has.

Workflow files are NOT skippable config. A workflow edit can delete the secret-scan step, widen permissions, or add a step that reads deployment secrets — i.e. it can disable the very gates protecting everything else. T1 so it is always reviewed. (Raised in operator review 2026-07-30; it was inherited as T2 from the generic defaults.)
